notes: Plural: tafels. In cafés you usually seat yourself; in restaurants wait to be shown a table.

examples.tl: Heeft u een tafel bij het raam?
examples.en: Do you have a table by the window?

notes: Usually just 'de kaart'. Careful: 'het menu' is a set meal of several courses.

examples.tl: Heeft u een Engelse menukaart?
examples.en: Do you have an English menu?

notes: Said 'RAY-kuh-ning'. You have to ask for it: staff will not bring it unasked. Plural: rekeningen.

examples.tl: Kunnen we de rekening krijgen?
examples.en: Can we get the bill?

notes: Said 'VAH-ter'. Tap water is 'kraanwater' and is excellent. Bottled: 'plat' (still) or 'bruisend / met prik' (sparkling).

examples.tl: Een fles water zonder prik, alstublieft.
examples.en: A bottle of still water, please.

notes: A plain 'koffie' is a small black cup, often with a biscuit. Koffie verkeerd = latte.

examples.tl: Twee koffie en een cappuccino, alstublieft.
examples.en: Two coffees and a cappuccino, please.

notes: Said 'tay'. 'Verse muntthee' (fresh mint tea) is on every café menu.

examples.tl: Een verse muntthee, alstublieft.
examples.en: A fresh mint tea, please.

notes: Order 'een biertje': a small draft lager, about 25 cl. 'Van de tap' = on tap. 'Speciaalbier' = craft and Belgian styles.

examples.tl: Welk bier heeft u van de tap?
examples.en: Which beer do you have on tap?

notes: Said 'vayn'. Rode wijn = red, witte wijn = white, huiswijn = house wine.

examples.tl: Een glas rode wijn, alstublieft.
examples.en: A glass of red wine, please.

notes: A filled roll, the standard Dutch lunch: broodje kaas, broodje gezond (ham, cheese, salad). Plural: broodjes.

examples.tl: Een broodje kaas om mee te nemen, alstublieft.
examples.en: A cheese sandwich to take away, please.

notes: Jong = young and mild, belegen = matured, oud = aged and sharp. Plural: kazen.

examples.tl: Mag ik de oude kaas proeven?
examples.en: May I taste the aged cheese?

notes: The bar snack, served by the plate with mustard. The inside is molten hot: bite carefully. Plural: bitterballen.

examples.tl: Een portie bitterballen, alstublieft.
examples.en: A portion of bitterballen, please.

notes: Two thin waffles glued with caramel syrup. Best warm from a market stall. Plural: stroopwafels.

examples.tl: Een verse stroopwafel van de markt is het lekkerst.
examples.en: A fresh stroopwafel from the market is the tastiest.

notes: Plate-sized and thin, sweet or savoury (spek = bacon, kaas, appel). Plural: pannenkoeken. Poffertjes = mini pancakes.

examples.tl: Ik neem de pannenkoek met spek en stroop.
examples.en: I'll have the pancake with bacon and syrup.

notes: 'Patat' in Amsterdam and the north, 'friet' in the south. The default sauce is mayonnaise.

examples.tl: Een grote friet met mayonaise, alstublieft.
examples.en: A large fries with mayonnaise, please.

notes: Raw salted herring with onion and pickle from a street stall. 'Hollandse Nieuwe' is the new-season catch, from June.

examples.tl: Een haring met uitjes, alstublieft.
examples.en: A herring with onions, please.

notes: Deep and chunky, served 'met slagroom' (with whipped cream).

examples.tl: Een appeltaart met slagroom en een koffie, graag.
examples.en: An apple pie with whipped cream and a coffee, please.

notes: Kipsaté (chicken satay with peanut sauce) is on most café menus. Plural: kippen.

examples.tl: Ik neem de kipsaté met friet.
examples.en: I'll have the chicken satay with fries.

notes: Said 'vlays'. Rundvlees = beef, varkensvlees = pork, gehakt = minced meat.

examples.tl: Ik eet liever vis dan vlees.
examples.en: I prefer fish to meat.

notes: Plural: vissen. Kibbeling = battered fried fish chunks, sold at fish stalls.

examples.tl: Wat is de vis van de dag?
examples.en: What is the fish of the day?

notes: Said 'vay-khuh-TAH-rees'. 'Vega' is the short form on menus; veganistisch = vegan.

examples.tl: Heeft u ook vegetarische gerechten?
examples.en: Do you also have vegetarian dishes?

notes: The all-purpose word of approval: food, weather, a nap. 'Lekker!' on its own is fine.

examples.tl: De soep is erg lekker.
examples.en: The soup is very tasty.

notes: Ik eet, wij eten; past: gegeten. 'Het eten' as a noun = the food.

examples.tl: Waar kunnen we hier goed eten?
examples.en: Where can we eat well around here?

notes: Ik drink; past: gedronken. 'Iets drinken' = to have a drink.

examples.tl: Zullen we ergens iets gaan drinken?
examples.en: Shall we go and have a drink somewhere?

notes: Ik bestel; past: besteld. In many cafés you order and pay at the bar, or by QR code on the table.

examples.tl: Kunnen we al bestellen?
examples.en: Can we order already?

notes: From 'PIN code'. Also means taking cash out of an ATM. Many places are card-only.

examples.tl: Kan ik hier pinnen?
examples.en: Can I pay by card here?

notes: Service is included. Rounding up or 5-10% for good table service is normal; nothing is expected at a counter.

examples.tl: Hoeveel fooi geef je hier meestal?
examples.en: How much do you usually tip here?

notes: Grilled ham-and-cheese sandwich, on every café lunch menu, served with ketchup. Plural: tosti's.

examples.tl: Een tosti ham-kaas, alstublieft.
examples.en: A ham and cheese toastie, please.

notes: Deep-fried ragout roll, from a snack-bar wall (FEBO) or as 'broodje kroket' with mustard. Plural: kroketten.

examples.tl: Twee broodjes kroket met mosterd, graag.
examples.en: Two croquette sandwiches with mustard, please.

notes: A café is a pub that also serves coffee and lunch. 'Bruin café' = old-style pub. A 'coffeeshop' sells cannabis, not coffee.

examples.tl: Zullen we naar het café op de hoek gaan?
examples.en: Shall we go to the bar on the corner?

notes: The tables outside a café. Plural: terrassen. Sit down and a waiter comes, or order inside if nobody does.

examples.tl: Zullen we op het terras gaan zitten?
examples.en: Shall we sit outside on the terrace?

notes: Albert Heijn (AH), Jumbo, Lidl. 'AH to go' at stations is the nearest thing to a convenience store. Plural: supermarkten.

examples.tl: Ik haal even water bij de supermarkt.
examples.en: I'll just get some water at the supermarket.

notes: Expect the counter-question 'Heeft u gereserveerd?' (do you have a reservation?).

examples.tl: Goedenavond. Een tafel voor twee, alstublieft. — Heeft u gereserveerd?
examples.en: Good evening. A table for two, please. — Do you have a reservation?

en: May I have the menu, please?
accept: Can I have the menu, please?
Could I see the menu, please?
notes: Locals mostly say 'Mag ik de kaart?' Many places have a QR code instead.

examples.tl: Mag ik de menukaart, alstublieft? — Natuurlijk, alstublieft.
examples.en: May I have the menu, please? — Of course, here you are.

notes: Waiters do not hover: catch their eye or raise a hand, then say this.

examples.tl: Pardon, we willen graag bestellen.
examples.en: Excuse me, we'd like to order.

notes: The -tje is how beer is ordered: you get a small draft lager. Two: 'twee biertjes' or 'twee bier'.

examples.tl: Een biertje en een witte wijn, alstublieft.
examples.en: A beer and a white wine, please.

en: May I have the bill, please?
accept: Can I have the check, please?
Can I have the bill, please?
notes: Or 'Mogen we afrekenen?' (can we pay?). In cafés you often just walk up and pay at the bar.

examples.tl: Mag ik de rekening, alstublieft? — Komt eraan.
examples.en: May I have the bill, please? — Coming right up.

notes: Splitting is completely normal here ('going Dutch'). Locals settle up afterwards with the Tikkie app.

examples.tl: Kunnen we apart betalen? — Ja hoor, wat had u?
examples.en: Can we pay separately? — Sure, what did you have?

en: May I have some tap water?
accept: Can I have some tap water?
Could I get some tap water?
notes: Kraan = tap. Tap water is excellent but not automatic: some restaurants charge a little or push bottled water.

examples.tl: Mag ik wat kraanwater? — Natuurlijk, ik breng een karaf.
examples.en: May I have some tap water? — Of course, I'll bring a carafe.

notes: Swap in: pinda's (peanuts), gluten, lactose, schaaldieren (shellfish), ei (egg).

examples.tl: Ik ben allergisch voor pinda's. Zit er pindasaus bij?
examples.en: I'm allergic to peanuts. Does it come with peanut sauce?

notes: 'Geen' because you are negating a noun. 'Ik ben vegetariër' = I am a vegetarian.

examples.tl: Ik eet geen vlees, maar wel vis.
examples.en: I don't eat meat, but I do eat fish.

accept: Does it have meat in it?
notes: 'Zit er ... in?' = does it contain ...? Zit er ei in? Zit er alcohol in?

examples.tl: Zit er vlees in de erwtensoep? — Ja, rookworst.
examples.en: Is there meat in the pea soup? — Yes, smoked sausage.

notes: Heerlijk is a notch above lekker. Said 'HAYR-luk'.

examples.tl: Dank u wel, het was heerlijk.
examples.en: Thank you, it was delicious.

notes: Said by waiters and by people at the table before starting. Reply 'dank u' or say it back.

examples.tl: Alstublieft, twee pannenkoeken. Eet smakelijk!
examples.en: Here you are, two pancakes. Enjoy your meal!

notes: Aanraden = to recommend, separable. Good for beer lists and cheese counters.

examples.tl: We twijfelen nog. Wat raadt u aan?
examples.en: We can't decide yet. What do you recommend?

notes: 'Nog een' = one more. Name the drink if it is not obvious: 'Nog een biertje.'

examples.tl: Nog een biertje, alstublieft.
examples.en: Another beer, please.

notes: Book ahead for dinner on Friday and Saturday; popular places fill up.

examples.tl: Ik heb gereserveerd voor twee personen om zeven uur.
examples.en: I have a reservation for two at seven o'clock.

notes: The waiter's question when clearing the plates. Answer: 'Ja, het was lekker.'

examples.tl: Heeft het gesmaakt? — Ja, heerlijk, dank u.
examples.en: Did you enjoy it? — Yes, delicious, thank you.

notes: What staff say when it is your turn to order, literally 'just say it'.

examples.tl: Zegt u het maar. — Een koffie verkeerd, alstublieft.
examples.en: Go ahead. — A latte, please.

notes: Asked at every counter and market stall after your first item.

examples.tl: Anders nog iets? — Nee, dank u.
examples.en: Anything else? — No, thank you.

notes: The standard answer to 'Anders nog iets?' when you are done ordering.

examples.tl: Anders nog iets? — Nee, dat was het.
examples.en: Anything else? — No, that's all.

notes: Kitchens often close around 9 or 10 pm, earlier than in the US or Asia.

examples.tl: Is de keuken nog open? — Ja, tot tien uur.
examples.en: Is the kitchen still open? — Yes, until ten.

notes: 'Met' alone = with mayonnaise. 'Patatje oorlog' = mayo, peanut sauce and onions. 'Zonder' = plain.

examples.tl: Een patatje met en een kroket, alstublieft.
examples.en: Fries with mayo and a croquette, please.

notes: Meenemen = to take along. Said after the order at coffee bars, bakeries and snack bars.

examples.tl: Een cappuccino om mee te nemen, alstublieft.
examples.en: A cappuccino to go, please.

notes: Asked at bakeries, coffee bars and snack bars. Answer: 'Hier opeten' or 'Meenemen, graag'.

examples.tl: Hier opeten of meenemen? — Meenemen, graag.
examples.en: Eat in or take away? — Take away, please.

notes: Or name the total you want to pay: 'Maak er maar twintig van' (make it twenty).

examples.tl: Dat is negentien euro. — Hier is twintig, laat maar zitten.
examples.en: That's nineteen euros. — Here's twenty, keep the change.
